__meta.what: Golden expectations for inputs JSON cannot express. Companion to canonical.json.
__meta.why: JSON has no undefined, no symbol keys, no prototype chain, and JSON.stringify(-0) is "0". Four of the behaviours most likely to fabricate a terms_hash mismatch are therefore unrepresentable in the main golden and are built in test/golden/edge-values.ts instead.
__meta.inputs: test/golden/edge-values.ts, keyed by name. One definition, no generator/test drift.
__meta.regenerate: The canonical column is hand-authored and is the oracle; the hash column is derived from it. To add a case: add a builder to test/golden/edge-values.ts, add a row here with a deliberately wrong hash, run test/core/canonical.test.ts, and copy the expected value out of the failure.

cases.name: negative_zero_scalar
cases.note: minus zero normalises to 0 - splitByBps returns -0 for negative remainders, so this reaches the ledger

cases.name: negative_zero_in_array
cases.note: every element normalises; a split result array cannot hash two ways

cases.name: negative_zero_as_object_value
cases.note: minus zero and zero as sibling values are one term

cases.name: undefined_value_omitted
cases.note: absent means absent: an undefined-valued key disappears rather than serialising as null

cases.name: undefined_only_key
cases.note: an object whose only key is undefined is the empty object

cases.name: absent_key_baseline
cases.note: the shape undefined_value_omitted must be identical to

cases.name: symbol_key_omitted
cases.note: symbol keys are invisible to Object.keys and are silently dropped, not rejected

cases.name: inherited_key_omitted
cases.note: only own enumerable keys serialise, so a prototype cannot smuggle a field into terms_hash

cases.name: deep_nested_32_arrays
cases.note: the depth guard counts arrays as well as objects; 33 throws, which is also the only cycle protection
